newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to decide on gene-modified maize on Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: EU to decide on gene-modified maize on Dec 18.

text.p: The European Commission plans to decide whether to allow imports of U.S. genetically modified maize on December 18, Commission Environment spokesman Peter Jorgensen said on Thursday.
It will act after receiving advice from EU committees on food, animal feed and pesticides as to whether Ciba-Geigy AG's gene modfified maize is safe.
The maize, which is authorised in the U.S., has been altered to resist the corn borer pest and certain weedkillers.
"The Commission is hoping to be able to take a view on the basis of the full range of scientific advice at its meeting on December 18," Jorgensen told Reuters.
Member states were warned in writing on November 27 that it was their responsibility to stop products which may contain genetically modified maize from entering the European Union.
But they could not unilaterally impose a ban.
"There is no question of any minister in any country deciding on his own account to ban genetically modified maize," the spokesman said.
The Commission said some gene modified maize may have been imported in foodstuffs.
"We accept that some imported processed products may have contained the cereal and we have reminded member states of their responsibility under Community law," the spokesman said.
U.S. exporters do not separate genetically modified maize from the ordinary variety.
